newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks drift higher at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks drift higher at midday.

text.p: U.S. stocks drifted modestly higher at an extremely quiet midsession as a narrow band of blue chip stocks continued to lead the market higher.

"The same stocks continue to go up," said Scott Bleier, chief investmemt strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "People are chasing yields and buying defensive, yield-oriented stocks like telecoms and oils."
The Dow Industrials rose 19 points to 6580 and the S&P 500 inched up a point to 758. The Nasdaq Composite also eked out a one point rise to stand at 1292.
The Dow was led by strong performances from its three oil components: Texaco Inc rose 1-1/4 to 100; Chevron Corp gained one to 67 and Exxon Corp rose 3/4 to 100-5/8.
AT&T Corp also extended its recent rally, adding 1/2 to 44-1/4.

Beyond the solid gains tallied by a few blue chips, the session was extremely quiet, with NYSE volume at a wafer-thin 150 million shares just after midday. Breadth was positive, with NYSE advancing issues ahead by about five-to-four.
With the majority of year-end tax-related selling likely over, analysts said the recent upswing in the market could spread to secondary stocks, but for now the buying interest remained very narrow.

"One would expect the laggards to pick up now that tax-loss selling is wrapping up," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "But generally speaking, buyers are very selective right now."
Technology shares were a mixed bag at midday, although one very slender segment of the tech stocks rallied sharply.
Computer service companies that specialize in developing software to deal with so-called "Year 2000" systems problems spiked higher as investors continued to show a ferocious appetite for the stocks.

One of the companies, Zitel Corp surged 7-5/8 to 68-7/8. Zitel shares have tripled in value since the start of December. Others included Acceler8 Technology Corp, up 6-5/8 to 28-1/8 and TSR Inc, up eight to 45-1/2.
Some analysts said the interest in the stocks was taking on manic proportions.

"This is like the biotech craze of 1991 and like when Iomega was up at 55," Bleier said, adding that the generally small tech companies currently focused on the millennium problem faced the ever-present risk that "some major mainframe maker will come up with the answer."
Among individual issues, Providian Corp fell 1-1/4 to 51-1/2 after agreeing to sell its insurance operations to Dutch insurer Aegon NV in a deal worth $3.5 billion.
NYSE-listed American Depositary Receipts in Aegon jumped 5-7/8 to 62-7/8.
